title: The Impossible Faithfulness
text:
Literary translation is often described as an impossible task, since every language carries rhythms, connotations, and cultural assumptions that resist faithful transfer. Translators must therefore decide, sentence by sentence, whether to preserve the literal meaning, the emotional tone, or the musicality of the original. Such choices are never neutral, for each one quietly reshapes how a foreign readership will perceive the author.

Consider the translator who renders an ironic remark as a sincere compliment: the words survive, yet the author's cutting intention vanishes entirely. Critics therefore judge a translation not by its accuracy alone but by whether it sustains the subtle tensions that gave the source text its vitality. A faithful translation, in this view, is one that makes the reader feel what the original made its readers feel.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what must translators decide sentence by sentence?
options: Whether to preserve the literal meaning, the emotional tone, or the musicality of the original
Whether to publish the translation in a foreign country
Whether the original author would approve of the work
Whether to omit the cultural references entirely

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what does the translator in the example turn an ironic remark into?
options: A factual statement about the author

questions.text: Why does the author describe translation choices as never neutral?
options: Because each choice changes how a foreign readership perceives the author
Because translators always work for political organisations
Because the source text is usually written in a neutral style
Because publishers prefer translations that are uniformly literal

questions.text: What does the second paragraph imply about the critics' view of a faithful translation?
options: It must match the original word for word
It should recreate the effect the original had on its readers
It should be shorter than the source text
It must avoid all ironic language

vocabulary.definition: the additional ideas and feelings a word suggests beyond its basic meaning
the pleasing rhythm and sound patterns of a piece of writing
saying one thing while meaning the opposite
accurately reflecting the original or the truth

paragraph_translations: A tradução literária costuma ser descrita como uma tarefa impossível, pois cada língua carrega ritmos, conotações e pressupostos culturais que resistem a uma transferência fiel. Os tradutores devem, portanto, decidir, frase a frase, se preservam o sentido literal, o tom emocional ou a musicalidade do original. Tais escolhas nunca são neutras, pois cada uma delas remodela silenciosamente a forma como um público estrangeiro percebe o autor.

Considere o tradutor que transforma uma observação irônica num elogio sincero: as palavras sobrevivem, mas a intenção cortante do autor desaparece por completo. Os críticos, por isso, julgam uma tradução não apenas pela sua precisão, mas por sustentar as tensões sutis que deram vitalidade ao texto de partida. Uma tradução fiel, nessa perspectiva, é aquela que faz o leitor sentir o que o original fazia sentir a seus leitores.
